answer: In an AI-agent economy, Sybil resistance emerges from a stake-weighted interaction trellis: each new identity must post a non-refundable bond and accumulate verified reciprocal work from existing agents before its influence score can climb toward the zenith of governance rights. Peer agents continuously mirror one another's contribution histories on-chain; forging dozens of fake identities therefore multiplies the capital lockup and the real computational service that must be delivered, rendering mass identity fabrication prohibitively expensive.
